howToTell: The Champ is a post-war design with a lower cabin and a slim fuselage; the wartime L-3/O-58 has a taller greenhouse, wider glazing and a rounded-looking tail.
The Super Cub has a slim, flat-sided cabin and a rounded tail; the Bird Dog is bigger, with a huge glazed rear cabin, spring-steel gear legs and a squarer tail.
The 180 seats four side-by-side with one rear window; the Bird Dog seats two in tandem under an enormous glazed rear cabin.
The L-4/J-3 Cub is a tiny narrow-fuselage airplane with a squared tail; the larger L-5 has a long glazed cabin and a six-cylinder cowl.
The PT-19/PT-26 Cornell is a low-wing monoplane trainer; the Stearman is a biplane with wires and struts between the two wings.
The Cornell has fixed gear, a light inline-style nose and a wire-free wing; the Texan is bigger with retractable gear and a big radial.
The Ryan PT-22 is a low-wing monoplane with big wheel spats; the Stearman is a biplane with interplane struts and wires.
The N3N is a Navy biplane that is usually yellow, with a smoother round cowl and a squatter body; the Stearman has a larger, more angular airframe and a bigger radial.
The Chipmunk is a smaller, lighter tailwheel airplane with a slim inline nose and fixed gear; the T-34 has a big flat-six nose and nose-wheel gear.
The BT-13 has fixed landing gear and a rounder, lower profile; the Texan has retractable gear and a taller canopy.
The DA20 is a lower, rounder composite with a longer glazed canopy; the P-Mentor has an upright fin, a straighter wing and an alloy-and-carbon look.
The L-29 has a rounder pot-bellied fuselage, straight wing with no tip tanks and a more bulbous nose; the L-39 is slimmer with a tapered wing and tip tanks.
The T-33 is a straight-wing, single-engine jet with big tip tanks and a very long canopy; the T-38 has swept wings, twin engines and a sleek pointed nose.
The Mirage F1 is a single-engine jet with a strongly swept high-set wing and a long pointed nose; the F-5 is a smaller twin-engine jet with a thin straight-edged wing and a shark nose.
The Tucano has a shorter nose and a lower, longer canopy; the T-6 Texan II has a taller canopy hump and a longer nose.
The Invader has a single tall fin and a straight mid wing with a sleek fuselage; the B-25 has twin fins and a gull wing.
The Sabreliner has a more strongly swept wing without tip tanks and a thin oval-windowed fuselage; the Learjet 35 has wingtip tanks and ventral delta fins.
The Iskra is a slimmer jet with a straight wing and wing-root intakes under a long single canopy; the L-39 has larger fuselage-side intakes and wingtip tanks.
The PC-7 has a three-blade propeller, a smaller airframe and a lower canopy; the T-6 Texan II has a four-blade propeller and a bigger airframe.
The Wildcat is a small single-seat fighter with a stubby body and narrow-track gear; the Avenger is a much bigger bomber with a bulbous fuselage.
The Firefly has a larger bubble canopy and fixed tricycle gear with fairings; the DA20 has a rounder canopy and a distinct tail shape.
The PC-9 is the smaller, sleeker airplane the T-6 Texan II was derived from, with a lower canopy and a smaller tail; the T-6 is larger and heavier-looking.
The Sea Fury has a big radial nose with a smooth round cowl and a five-blade propeller; the Mustang has a pointed inline nose and a belly scoop.
The Thunderbolt is much bigger with a barrel-shaped fuselage, a round radial nose and an oval chin intake; the Mustang is slim with a pointed inline nose and a belly scoop.
The Yak-18T seats four under a long bubble canopy; the Yak-52 is a two-seat tandem trainer with a smaller canopy.
The Yak-18T seats four in a long cabin; the CJ-6 is a two-seat tandem trainer.
